questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The language spoken and the geographical location

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was fun, but the courses were very easy. 300 courses at UBC are basically fake, I mean they are equivalent to first year classes back home. Which means they are great if you want to do as little as possible but it get's boring fast. 400 classes is a massive jump in difficulty, it isn't more difficult than back home it's the exact same level, but because of midterms and the like you end up having a lot of work all the time, I wouldn't recommend taking more than 2 of those if you want any free time. The social life really doesn't exist if you don't get on campus housing. I was lucky to be going with a friend and met some people there. But I would almost advise people not to go if they don't get on campus housing, which is funny since you don't know if you get it until like 2 months before. All in all the experience is what you make of it, people are very young and the social aspect isn't all that great outside of the housing you get, something to keep in mind.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, don't remember having any problems with anything.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an introduction day in which everything you needed to know was explained

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very difficult, very expensive, twice as expensive. Me and a friend booked through Airbnb, you get a discount on loing term stays, but if you are living alone, it's going to financially ruin you.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's a very different experience. Most people only really hang out with the people who they live with because there really isn't really anything social in the classes themselves, most people sit by them selves not just international students, studying in Canada is very individual much more than here. I was going with a friend which really saved the experience. We also made friends with the other danish students and a couple of friends outside that, but you have to make an active effort to make friends if you live off campus. Me and my friends had it best, many of the other danish students who went alone and lived off campus, did not have the best of times. I frankly wouldn't recommend going if you don't get on campus housing, unless you're fine with doing stuff on your own.

Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The classes could pretty "easily" be found online and you got plenty of messages on how to sign up for classes, overall it wasn't too difficult, don't expect to get the classes you want exactly though, there is a lot of competition for classes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: No idea, I just followed the messages from the uni and so on and didn't have all that many problems but I also wasn't dependent on getting specific classes and had a lot of wiggle room.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not that, got 1 out of 3 classes I wanted, but it was the most important one so that's something.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the mails and stuff you get from the uni, then you'll do fine.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 300 courses are waaaaayy too easy, think 1'st semester. 400 classes is a massive jump think about appropriate for 5th semester at home, but with a "heavier" workload in that you have at least 2 midterms and 1 exam in every class, meaning you end up with 4 classes having essentially 12 exams. So 400 aren't more difficult, just the level you're used to, but with a different workload.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty similar, no "hold timer" though at least not in anyway that resembles back home, so very individual learning, essentially only lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: 333 was great, amazing professor, don't touch 345 with a 10 foot pole, the professor is the worst I've ever had. 355 was also good. 371 was very boring and by far the easiest class, which is saying something.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is pretty expensive to make yourself, takeout and restaurants are considerably cheaper than back home, so you end up spending a lot on food, especially if you want anything remotely healthy since the quality in general isn't that great unless you go to special stores.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The social clubs were pretty interesting, I highly recommend the outdoor club and the surf club and the ski club. The surf club hosts a trip to tofino which is very fun and the outdoor club has stuff to do every week, so you can really get out a lot, and the people who run it are psychopaths in the best way possible

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds, there are like a thousand clubs, if you have an interest, there is a club for it, but some of them are pretty niche, and it isn't as chill as one might think, the people who are in these clubs make their hobbies a fundament part of their personality. If you imagine the surf club they live up to all the stereotypes that you have, and the outdoor club as well. All the clubs are very stereotypical of what you think, they live up to their image in an almost comical sense.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: As I said, the surf trip to tofino, the outdoor club's very week activities and also their "rock" part which is a rock climbing getaway, very fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: If you are going in the 5th semester as most people probably are, PACK your September and early October with stuff, don't ever have a weekend free, because the sun and good weather disappears fast, and when it's gone it's gone. I highly recommend going to the Campbell river to see grizzly bears and the salmon run which happens in the end of September start of October every year, it's sick. Go to panorama ridge, and again go in September or early October, just hike as much as possible, once the weather is bad, you won't be getting out, it will be too cold to do any longer hikes, so really really take advantage of of the first month and a half, stuff it with as many activities as possible.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy, although they don't have a party culture at all, if you want to have fun nightlife Vancouver is NOT for you, that place is ass concerning the night life scene, and everybody knows it. If you ask the locals what they do they will consistently answer "nothing" because there genuinly isn't anything.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: you have to join a club and preferably multiple it's a must especially if you don't get on campus housing, and even if you do you need to be lucky with the people living with you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: none.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get on campus housing, join a club, go outside as much as possible, if you spend a single weekend not hiking the first month and a half you're wasting your time, because it's only an option in the beginning.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: the travels I went on, I went to San Fran, Seattle and New York ,that was fun. lot of people go to Banff but I had been already, but again you can only go to Banff and those places before the 20th of October basically where after that it's over.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding people older than 18 and who were worth hanging out with.
